Mia: ran a quick int4 probe on customer 'Iris' LoRA (iris-lora-v3). Seeing numeric formatting regressions and one truncation in long-table prompt. Quick summary: pass 50/60, numeric-integrity 0.87 vs float16 0.99.

Devin: can you paste the run command + top failures?

Mia: command:
```
./bench/run_quick_eval --model iris-lora-v3 --quant=int4 --prompts=customers/iris/smoke_prompts.json --out=/tmp/iris_int4.json --batch=8
```
Failures (redacted): 1) id12: "$1,234.56" -> "$1,234." (truncated) 2) id19: "42.0" -> "42 .0" (extra space) 3) id33: long table row truncated after 128 tokens.

Arjun: tokenizer mismatch or int4 rounding. Did you force same tokenizer/merges?

Mia: yes, used customers/iris/tokenizer.json. Also tried bias-correction toggle. No change.

Devin: include KV logs around token 120-130 to check cache drift.

Mia: KV excerpt:
```
kv[118] = <tok "$">
kv[119] = <tok "1">
kv[120] = <tok ",">
kv[121] = <tok "234">
kv[122] = <tok ".">
kv[123] = <tok "56">
kv[124] = <tok "\n">
kv[125] = <tok "$">  # next row, dp lower by ~0.12 vs baseline
kv[126] = <tok "2">
```

Arjun: looks like per-channel scale issue in int4. Two experiments: enable per-channel rescale, or run a tiny bias-fix calibration.

Mia: enabled per-channel rescale -> numeric-integrity 0.95, pass 56/60, truncation fixed on repro.

Sara: perf impact?

Mia: ~4% latency increase at 1024 context, within Iris SLO.

Devin: action: Arjun open model profile PR to recommend int4+per-channel rescale; Mia run full quickpack and upload. I'll notif customer.
